newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell says EU cannot block Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell says EU cannot block Boeing merger.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp said Friday the European Union does not have the power to block its planned merger with Boeing Co.
"They do not have absolute jurisdiction to block the merger," said general counsel Mark Kuhlmann in response to shareholder questions at the company's annual meeting here.
"They could institute fines or take other similar actions if they disapprove the merger," Kuhlmann added.

The fines, if imposed by the EU, could make it difficult for the merged company to compete in Europe. "But we're confident that we're going to be able to work out the issues with the EU," McDonnell spokesman Larry McCracken said later.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has said that one condition of the merger would be for Boeing to drop exclusive sales agreements with airline companies.

McDonnell officials said earlier this month that it did not expect European Union or U.S. Federal Trade Commission issues to pose any obstacles to the merger. McDonnell officials have said they expect the deal to be completed around August 1.

Kuhlmann told the annual meeting today that McDonnell's discussions with European Union officials about the merger will continue. "We are fully are confident that we will resolve those concerns," he added.
After the meeting, McDonnell chief executive Harry Stonecipher said the ultimate decision on the merger will belong to the FTC, which will likely influence the EU.
